source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), Department of Agricultural Extension — trifold "វិធីបណ្តុះកូនល្ហុង" (Method for Raising Papaya Seedlings), citing Training Module on Fruit Tree Production (2013) and a farmer's field experience from Kampong district, Preah Vihear province (2012)
text:
For raising papaya seedlings, farmers should first select seeds from a healthy, true-to-type mother tree — not a hybrid — that shows clear, consistent characteristics and has flowered/fruited only once. Choose a fruit that has ripened fully while still on the tree, then pick it and remove the seeds.

After removing the seeds, dry them in the shade rather than in direct sun. Select only the plump, black, and glossy seeds for planting; discard shriveled, pale, or discolored seeds, since these indicate poor viability. The good seeds should be spread out on a tray or plate and shade-dried for 2–3 days before moving on to germination.

The source also notes that seedlings should be raised from seed with a germination rate of at least 60% to ensure a productive nursery batch.
